rule: The lower half of the head circle is divided into four equal bands by three lines: eyebrows on the first, upper eyelashes on the second, irises on the third.
The chin sits about a quarter of the circle's diameter below the bottom of the circle.
There is a blank space of one eye's width between the two eyes.
The mouth is midway between the bottom of the circle (where the nose rests) and the tip of the jaw.
The top of the ear is about level with the middle of the eye and its bottom is not quite as low as the mouth line.
In three-quarter view a gently curving vertical centre line runs from the chin up to the brow line, off to one side.
In three-quarter view the eyes, eyebrows, nose and mouth all touch the curving centre line, and the far eyebrow is not directly above the far eye but off to one side.
In profile the face line goes to the nose tip and then down to the chin with small bumps for the lips midway down.
In profile the eye sits between the 2nd and 3rd lines, close to but not touching the circle edge, and the mouth is near the midpoint between nose and chin.
For an adult face the chin is about a third of the circle's diameter below the circle.
An adult's eyebrows and eyes are a full line higher than a young character's, and the nose is more fully rendered.
In the adult three-quarter view the mouth is a little less than halfway between chin and nose, just outside the circle edge.
In a cheerful expression the bottoms of the eyes are flattened, as if the cheeks rise.
In ecstatic joy the eyes are squeezed shut and the bottom of the mouth may be left unrendered.
Determination shows clenched teeth and a break in the line surrounding the mouth.
Surprise shows small irises floating in the whites of the eyes and a small open gasping mouth.
Most manga artists ink with comparatively thin lines that do not vary much in width.
